content.intro: Reusable Libraries is lesson 147 in The .NET Project and Package Ecosystem. A reproducible .NET project describes target frameworks, settings, and dependencies in version-controlled files so another machine can restore and build the same code.
content.why_it_matters: Reproducible builds depend on explicit project settings and consistent dependency management. This lesson focuses on reusable libraries and shows how to verify the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small C# example that demonstrates reusable libraries. Change one input or implementation detail, predict the result, then check it locally and explain one edge case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates reusable libraries rather than only repeating its definition.
The result is checked locally or against a clearly documented reference output.
At least one relevant boundary, invalid-input case, or compatibility condition is considered.
hints: List the assumptions and expected behavior for reusable libraries before editing the code.
Change one variable or rule at a time; keep the previous output for comparison.
If behavior differs, confirm the compiler/target framework and consult the linked official documentation.
content.solution_notes: Suggested approach: identify the expected input and output, start from the smallest example, use the feature only where it clarifies the rule, and verify both a typical case and a boundary/failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the feature works identically on every target
common_mistakes.why: Language syntax, libraries, and runtime support are version-dependent.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the target framework and official versioned reference before using the feature.

common_mistakes.why: Boundary values, malformed input, and failure states often expose the real bug.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one typical input and one boundary or invalid case to the manual or automated checks.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating sample output as proof that the code ran
common_mistakes.why: The course reader uses static reference output for C# because it has no C# execution runner.
common_mistakes.fix: Run the snippet in a local .NET project or a separately isolated execution service.
